name: Hydroxypropyl gluconamide

card.summary: A glucose-derived hair ingredient used in bond-repair and strengthening treatments to help damaged, bleached or colored hair look and feel stronger and smoother.
card.note: Usually sold as a blend; supplier claims are the main published description.

quick.overview:
Hydroxypropyl gluconamide is a cosmetic ingredient made by reacting gluconolactone with 3-aminopropanol [2]. It is listed as a humectant and hair-conditioning agent and appears in many bond-repair and 'plex'-style hair products [2].

Its supplier markets it as a glucose-based chemistry for hair strengthening, sold as a blend with hydroxypropylammonium gluconate, to improve strength and manageability of damaged hair [1].
quick.mechanism: According to its supplier, it penetrates into the hair cortex and forms new hydrogen and ionic bonds that support the damaged internal keratin structure [1]. This is the manufacturer's description of the mechanism.
quick.risks: Published safety and performance data are not provided on the ingredient listings consulted. It is a rinse-off and leave-on cosmetic ingredient, and standard product-label guidance applies.

chain: Forms hydrogen and ionic bonds with keratin
angle.text: It is used in bond-repair shampoos, conditioners and treatments aimed at making chemically damaged hair look healthier and hold together better during styling and coloring.

lead: Hydroxypropyl gluconamide is a cosmetic hair-care ingredient derived from gluconolactone, a glucose-based compound, and 3-aminopropanol [2]. Its INCI-listed functions are humectant and hair conditioning [2].

It is best known as part of Fiberhance BM, a supplier blend with hydroxypropylammonium gluconate that is described as a patented chemistry for hair strengthening [1]. The supplier says it penetrates the cortex, forms new hydrogen and ionic bonds that support damaged keratin, and improves strength and manageability [1]. Ingredient databases list many bond-repair products containing it, including products from Bond Bar, OGX and Schwarzkopf [2].

paras: It appears in bond-building shampoos, conditioners and leave-in or pre-color treatments aimed at damaged and chemically processed hair [2].

sections.h: Mechanism as described by the supplier
paras: The supplier describes glucose-derived molecules that enter the hair shaft and form new bonds with the damaged internal keratin structure, supporting strength and ease of management [1].
